title: Quietly Quenched Chinese Lamb Bao
description: A herbal and crisp Chinese Xinjiang dish featuring lamb, cream of tartar, and lamination-puff pastry, served in a cataplana vessel to help cure hangovers, this low-glycemic-friendly recipe is perfect for a comforting meal. The combination of flavors and textures will quietly quench your hunger and soothe your senses.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, whisk together cream of tartar, cumin, coriander, and a pinch of salt.
Add the lamb pieces to the bowl and toss to coat with the spice mixture.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the lamb until browned on all sides.
In a separate skillet, sauté the sliced onion and grated ginger until the onion is translucent.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for an additional minute.
Roll out the lamination-puff pastry to a large rectangle, about 1/4 inch thick.
Spoon the lamb and onion mixture onto one half of the pastry, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling and press the edges to seal.
Place the pastry in a cataplana vessel and brush the top with cataplana sauce.
Bake the bao in the preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.
